LOGIC ADVENTURE 18 · CLASS 30

Fox’s Logic Picnic

Age 4–5 YearsClass 30 · LogicSkill Two-clue logic

A puzzle piece and a food each name one basket — match both clues to find it.

Play the puzzle game ↓Print the worksheet ↓Play with a finger, a stylus or a mouse. Instructions are spoken aloud.
PLAY · TWO-CLUE LOGIC

Fox’s Logic Picnic

Fox packed three picnics! Each clue shows a puzzle piece and a food. The piece’s colour matches the basket, and the food tells you what’s inside. Tap the basket that fits both clues!

A green piece and an apple. Which basket fits both clues?

A yellow piece and a cupcake. Which basket fits both clues?

A red piece and a cookie. Which basket fits both clues?

Three picnics matched!

Green apple basket, yellow cupcake basket, red cookie basket — both clues every time!

FOR GROWN-UPS

Why this adventure helps.

This is early deductive reasoning: neither clue alone picks the basket, and saying it aloud — “green… and an apple… so the green apple basket!” — is the skill. The game mixes the baskets so the answer never sits in the same spot.

Illustration note: The real logic is two clues at once: the puzzle piece gives the basket colour and the food gives the contents. Each row always offers one right-colour-wrong-food and one right-food-wrong-colour basket, so both clues are needed.

Prefer paper? The Fox’s Logic Picnic worksheet prints the same puzzle with room to draw, sort and circle — and a grown-up answer line. Printing never marks anything complete.
